summary.text: A girl aged 9 years and 8 months came to a children’s clinic with a delay in changing teeth and some cavities, with no relevant systemic impairment reported. Examination showed short stature with shortened upper and lower limbs, overweight, and a significant delay in tooth eruption, with carious lesions on four primary teeth.

Panoramic radiography showed no change in tooth number, forming roots of unerupted permanent teeth and only discrete resorption of deciduous roots. Hand and wrist radiography gave a bone age of 5 years and 9 months. A geneticist ruled out any syndromic alteration, and an endocrinologist diagnosed hypothyroidism by hormone dosage.

Treatment was multidisciplinary, initially levothyroxine sodium hormone replacement, and dental care with restorations of teeth 54 and 64 in resin-modified glass ionomer cement. Extraction of teeth 85 and 75 and a Nance lingual arch space maintainer were part of the proposed dental treatment. Intraoral photos after 6 months of treatment show birth of the maxillary and mandibular central incisors, upper lateral exfoliation and an installed space maintainer. One year after the first visit, eruption corresponding to the chronology of age was verified, and the authors report an improved quality of life.

ambiguities.description: The Figure 4 caption dates the panel A photos "after 6 months of treatment" (anchor: treatment), while the text cites Figure 4A,B for the return "One year after the first visit" (anchor: first visit). The anchors differ and the interval between first visit and treatment start is not stated, so both can hold; whether the photos are from one session or two is not stated. Panel B has no caption time.
